terminology.title: Terminology
terminology.subtitle: Rename anything the app says, in both languages. A change reaches everyone the moment you save it — nothing is deployed, and nothing is lost: clear a box and the built-in wording comes straight back.
terminology.settingsHint: The wording of every label, title, button and message — in English and Arabic.
terminology.adminOnly: Only an admin can change the app's wording.
terminology.notInstalled: This project doesn't have the label overrides table yet, so the built-in wording is in use everywhere and nothing here can be saved. See RUNBOOK 4.1.

sectionHint.entryFields: The words that name a field — on an item, in a form, in a filter.

sectionHint.healthStates: On track, going quiet, overdue, blocked — and the status, priority and type words beside them.

sectionHint.emptyStates: What a list says when there is nothing in it.
sectionHint.messages: Toasts, confirmations, hints, and everything a screen says when something goes wrong.

terminology.searchPlaceholder: A word you can see on screen
terminology.searchHint: Searches the built-in wording, your wording, the section name and the key.
terminology.placeholderDefault: Leave empty to keep the built-in wording
terminology.blankMeansDefault: An empty box is never an empty label — it means the built-in wording.
terminology.bidiNote: In Arabic, the values the app fills in — a name, a date, a number — and any range like ⁦3–10⁩ are fenced automatically when you save, so they read in the right order. The rest of what you type is stored exactly as you typed it.
terminology.pluralTitle: This one changes with the number
terminology.pluralHint: English picks between two forms. Arabic picks between six — for 0, 1, 2, 3–10, 11–99 and 100 or more. Fill in the forms you want to change and leave the rest empty.
terminology.pluralExactHint: This form covers one number only, so it may leave the number out: “Every day”, not “Every 1 day”.
terminology.pluralRangeHint: This form covers many numbers, so it has to keep the one that says which.
terminology.savedToast: Saved. Everyone sees the new wording.

resetAllConfirm.one: Put the one label you renamed back to its built-in wording? Nothing else changes, and you can rename it again.
resetAllConfirm.other: Put all {count} labels you renamed back to their built-in wording? Nothing else changes, and you can rename them again.

resetAllDone.one: 1 label is back to its built-in wording.
resetAllDone.other: {count} labels are back to their built-in wording.

terminology.errLoadHint: The built-in wording is showing meanwhile, so nothing on screen is wrong. Try again.
terminology.errSave: That wording didn't save — the row is back as it was.
terminology.errResetAll: Couldn't reset them. Nothing was changed.
terminology.errTokenMissing: The built-in wording has ⁦{token}⁩ in it and yours doesn't. Put it back — it stands for a value the app fills in.
terminology.errTokenUnknown: There is no ⁦{token}⁩ in the built-in wording, so it would show on screen exactly as you typed it, braces and all.
terminology.errCountMissing: The ⁦{category}⁩ form covers more than one number, so it has to keep {count} — that is where the number goes.
terminology.errUnreachableCategory: This language never uses the ⁦{category}⁩ form, so nobody would ever read what you type here.
terminology.errPluralWhole: This wording changes with the number, so it can't be written as one sentence. Edit the forms underneath instead.
terminology.errUnknownKey: That label is not part of this app any more, so there is nothing to rename.
terminology.errTooLong: That wording is too long to store. A label is a few words, not a paragraph — shorten it and save again.
terminology.errBadKey: That line names something that is not a label key, so it can’t be saved. It is usually a file that was edited by hand.
terminology.ioHint: Download every change as one file, draft a wording pass in it, then load it back. Only the keys in the file change — everything else is left alone.
terminology.exportEmpty: There is nothing to download — no wording has been changed yet.

importSkipped.one: 1 key in the file is not part of this app and was skipped.
importSkipped.other: {count} keys in the file are not part of this app and were skipped.

importConfirmBody.one: One label changes for everyone, the moment you confirm. You can put it back afterwards — that row on its own, or every change at once.
importConfirmBody.other: {count} labels change for everyone, the moment you confirm. You can put them back afterwards — one row on its own, or every change at once.

terminology.importNoChange: Every wording in this file is already the wording in use, so there is nothing to apply.

importRejected.one: One line in this file can't be applied, so none of it is. Fix it and load the file again — nothing here has changed.
importRejected.other: {count} lines in this file can't be applied, so none of it is. Fix them and load the file again — nothing here has changed.

importRejectedMore.one: And one more, not shown here.

terminology.errImportParse: That file couldn't be read. It has to be the file this screen downloads.
terminology.errImportShape: That file is readable, but it isn't a wording export — it needs a key with an English or an Arabic wording under it.
terminology.errImport: Couldn't apply the file. Nothing was changed.
terminology.noResultsHint: This searches the built-in wording and yours, in both languages, plus the section name and the key. If you are looking for something you already renamed, try turning off “Only what I changed”.
terminology.noChangesHint: Every label is showing its built-in wording. Turn this off to see all of them.
